Train sabotage is crippling Cape Towns economy

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
only 8 trains on the central line to carry 200 000 people to work, its crippling the Western cape economy

Unique Selling Point:
Cape Town’s Metro Rail is under siege. 33 carriages have been destroyed in the last 4 months alone costing R140 million rand in damages. Since 2015 149 carriages have been destroyed. The last attempt at burning the trains happen this Tuesday when a seat was set alight just after they had reopened platform 3 and 4 after a fire on 21st July destroyed 6 carriages and 160 meters of copper cable. Fortunately commuters caught the perpetrator. The impact of thhis sabatague is having a worse effect on the Western cape economy than the drought. Speculation is rife as to who could be behind this concerted campaign and the arrest this week of a man trying to set carriages alight in Cape Town station has given investigators some hope that it may lead them to who is behind this. Some say its a third force, others say its a way to win back the Western cape from the DA.

Summary:
This is just the latest in a sustained campaign to sabotage Cape Town’s rail system, in January the central line was closed for 6 weeks forcing 1000’s of rail commuters onto the roads. To date no one can work out who or why there is this sustained attack on the trains. Some say it’s to cripple the DA in the Western Cape, others say it’s disgruntled Union members.
On the Cape Flats line it’s clear that copper thieves are the main culprits for train sabotage and Metro rail are now building a massive wall from Bontehewel to Netreg Heideveld linked to Nyanga which is costing R70 million rand. This is to separate the line from encroaching shacks and therefoe easy access for copper thieves. Copper thieves are well armed and organised syndicates that attack railway repair staff. They have to work under heavily armed security but no sooner they do a repair it is stolen. Copper thieves are even digging under vendors stalls to access the copper.


Further information:
The situation is so out of hand that the City of Cape Town has been negotiating with PRASA to take over the railway lines because it’s having such a disastrous impact on the Western Cape economy as well as the over- burdened road system. This week they announced that 100 new railway peace officers would be employed. The problem with railway police is that they cannot travel on the trains with any firearms because they are so over- crowded that they will be attacked for their weapons.
People are losing their jobs because they are consistently late. 86% of businesses in the Western Cape have said it is affecting their sustainability because they cannot keep up production schedule. The roads are so congested that has a further knock on effect on their bottom -line
There should be 88 carriages running but there are only 45. On the central line there should be 33 and they only have 8. People are not only losing their jobs but people are losing their lives. A woman died in the train fire at Ottery station and another woman sustained severe injuries.

Press Release:


Metrorail Sabotage
With 39 train carriages set alight and destroyed in just the last four months, Cape Town’s Metrorail is under siege and it will cost R51 million to recover from the damage. Since 2015, 149 carriages have been destroyed and now only eight trains remain to carry thousands of people to work, crippling the Western Cape economy. Investigators believe that there is a sustained campaign to sabotage the city’s rail system. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Script: The torching and sabotage of trains in the Western Cape has reached crisis point, people are losing their lives, and it’s threatening the economy.
Link “Just to give you an idea of the destruction 33 carriages have been burnt since the beginning of the year and 15 this month alone the cost running to 10’s of millions
Script: The crisis has been building over years, but things become critical in the last two. The latest incident was at Cape Town Station, 2 carriages were torched and 160 meters of copper cable destroyed. Brett Herron is the Mayoral Committee member for Transport.
Brett “The service looks like and feels like it's on the brink of collapse.
Script: this week there was another taxi strike and the burning of two Golden Arrow buses, causing havoc once again.
Brett “There seems to be some sinister force that is hell bent on destroying our public transport network
Zimisele “Its coming from bad to worse its actually completely failing everyone
Script: 149 trains have been destroyed since 2015.
Zimisele “ There are never trains on time there ever since I think it’s been two years now if the trains are there they are never safe
Script: Cape Town needs 88 train sets, but it’s down to only 45. People are losing their jobs because they’re constantly late.
Elizabeth: “The boss thinks we are lying to them because you can’t say everyday it was the train its late it can’t be late every day
Script: Emile Butler-O’Brien travels first class paying over R500 a month for his ticket, but he says the situation is no better. This is a fight he filmed of 1st class passengers trying to defend their space against desperate 3rd class commuters
Emile “People trampling over each other just to get onto the train. … I have had my watch ripped off my hand. It's just crazy.
Derek ‘What train are we catching… Emile 3.52 on platform 10
Script” But that can change at the last minute, and then it’s a mad scramble
Derek “there has been a platform change to platform 12 so we late
Script: And then the train only left half an hour later
Emile “Since the beginning of this year with train delays from 60 Minutes to 120 minutes 180 min and then cancellations
Link “As you may notice the doors hardly close they hardly close or if they close its stuck but how dangerous is this extremely you can get pushed off if the train goes like this you can fall out , especially when it’s over crowded
Script: Conditions are so bad that the Rail Safety Regulator only issued PRASA with a temporary extension till the end of August.
Link “well it may be overcrowded in the carriages but for some it’s a questions of hanging on outside and you can see how dangerous that is
Script: But once we set off it was announced that the train had changed routes and wasn’t going to the station we needed, Emile told us this happens regularly
Derek “That was quite an experience I wouldn’t like to do it every working day of my life I can tell you
Script: The next day we tried the Central line which comes from Khayelitsha. There should be 33 trains on this route but they are down to 8.
Sapho “The sun is now out and I have standing here for an hour
Script: We were hoping to travel with film student Sapho Wulana but when the train arrived it was bursting with people.
Sapho “It's a normal thing that a lot of people have lost their lives while on the trains when it's very packed with the guys who go up the trains and most of them in between the carriages. So it's normal, nobody nobody sees it as a bad thing anymore.
Derek “What’s the mood of people
Sapho “The people are very angry especially in the mornings the crowds. …people wake up very early to be on the trains and then the train delays and stuff and they have to go to work. the train just stops in the middle of nowhere for hours and there's nothing you can do.
Script: Cable thieves can be seen here brazenly ripping out cable in full view of commuters. Copper theft and crime brought the Central line to a stand still for 6 weeks in January, forcing people to take taxis at twice the price.
Link: A single train during peak time carries about 2000 passengers so when half of them are knocked out of the system those commuters have one alternative they take to the roads
Brett” It is now doubled it is now four hours in peak period as a as opposed to two hours
Script: Janine Myburgh Chair of the Cape Chamber of Commerce says the gridlock is hitting business hard
Janine “But people are not going to invest in an area where there staff cannot come to work. People are looking to move out of the area the CBD potentially
Brett “The impact on our economy at between two point seven billion and three point eight billion rand per annum.
Script; Metro Regional Manager Richard Walker is the first to admit that the commuters are taking the brunt of the collapse, but he says they are experiencing an unprecedented crime wave
Richard “We've never seen it before. And you know I'm talking of areas where even police can't go in. We also need to deal with the issue of whilst we are modernizing the system. We are we are going to be bringing new trains. Part of our recovery we would go in and put a couple hundred metres of cables and tomorrow it's gone
Derek “Whose responsibility is it to protect the cables.
Richard Walker “Yeah it is our responsibility. But when you have a situation that the very security that you are deploying comes under attack … a security guard that was shot while on duty there guarding the assets in area central.
Script: But rail security is in complete disarray, the guards are ineffective, unarmed or totally absent and lots of CCTV cameras aren’t working
Sapho “ I do fear for my life on the train because sometimes even if you're just sitting there's no windows sometimes just sitting and you'll on this station will just see people getting in by the windows and they are packed on you and you they jump on you…. There's a lot of robbery now going on on the trains because of the security. It's just nothing's happening.
Link: it was recently announced that 100 new railway security officers would be trained and deployed to prevent violence and arson on the trains but with 1000’s of commuters can they really make a difference
Script: JP Smith mayoral committee member for safety and security says they will be highly trained and target hotspots to protect the commuters and the trains
JP “There is over R40 million rand being spent on this additional law enforcement linking it to CCTV camera footage and our information gathering so we can offer a more information intelligence driven policing
Derek But they can’t be armed because the trains are too crowded
JP “ There will be a mix and match of uniformed and ununiformed and armed to get the right outcome
Link “Nobody can say why there are these sustained attacks on the trains some say it’s to cripple the Western Cape Government, others that it is disgruntled security guards or even that these torching’s are orchestrated by taxi bosses
Zimisele “Once the service is not there you know people become disgruntled so the first line of attack is to attack what is in front of you
Elizabeth “The people burn, the people are angry because I think PRASA isn’t doing their work
Brett “So what we’re seeing was fires being started just as trains are arriving in stations and a commuter crowd gets off the train and the train is set alight and the pattern just seemed to be too consistent too well organized that it could be just frustrated a random crime.
JP “I think there is a purposeful and concerted effort to make the city ungovernable in the run up to the next elections
Script: And the arson isn’t only destroying the carrying capacity, it’s left one woman dead and another scarred for life
Link “ 2 months ago Leigh Jansen boarded the train here at Southfield to head to her job in the city to her surprise the carriage was virtually empty apart from one other women passenger
Leigh “ I said Sis there is a fire in the train and she completely panicked …we both darted to the inter-leading door of the train and as we grabbed on there it was locked.
Derek “You were trapped.
Leigh” I am not ready to die this is a train I opened the window which was this big. I put my head through there and I just let go and I've dropped straight onto my face. I cracked two of my teeth.
Script: The other woman died, and Leigh spent two months in hospital
Derek Are you left with bitterness and hatred.
Leigh “ I am not bitter at all I am just so grateful to be alive.. I didn't care what I was going to look like afterwards…..
Script: An arsonist was caught this week which they hope will give them some leads, and 150 copper thieves have been arrested in the last few months
Richard . “Now we're building a wall a concrete slab wall which we've tested Nyanga at a cost of 70 million plus and we're going to fence off the entire area from Bontehewel right through to Nyanga
Derek “ You sound desperate .
Richard “ there are actually bucket shops owned by gang bosses in that area and they are using the desperate situation of individuals sending them they're paying a pittance
Janine “ The police's intelligence is not up to scratch they need to ask who benefits from the export of this scrap copper
Script: And Government needs to step up
Janine “That is why we asked the Minister of Trade and Industry to put a ban on you can say a moratorium that scrap copper should not be exported.
Derek “ Does the city actually want to take over the rail service.
Brett” It is our national government policy that all land based public transport should be operated or managed by local government. The new minister in Nzimande in, his view is that rail should be assigned to local government. Let's hope.
Walker: Government has taken the decision 172 billion to renew the rail system nationally the Western Cape will see 9 billion of that invested over the next three years.
Script: And in the meantime, commuters are stressed out of their minds
Emile “From 12 in the afternoon I start getting stressed about trains being delayed, trains being cancelled. I have no idea what time I am going to be home tonight

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): only 8 trains on the central line to carry 200 000 people to work, its crippling the Western cape economy
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Cape Town’s Metro Rail is under siege. 33 carriages have been destroyed in the last 4 months alone costing R140 million rand in damages. Since 2015 149 carriages have been destroyed. The last attempt at burning the trains happen this Tuesday when a seat was set alight just after they had reopened platform 3 and 4 after a fire on 21st July destroyed 6 carriages and 160 meters of copper cable. Fortunately commuters caught the perpetrator. The impact of thhis sabatague is having a worse effect on the Western cape economy than the drought. Speculation is rife as to who could be behind this concerted campaign and the arrest this week of a man trying to set carriages alight in Cape Town station has given investigators some hope that it may lead them to who is behind this. Some say its a third force, others say its a way to win back the Western cape from the DA.
metadata.Summary: This is just the latest in a sustained campaign to sabotage Cape Town’s rail system, in January the central line was closed for 6 weeks forcing 1000’s of rail commuters onto the roads. To date no one can work out who or why there is this sustained attack on the trains. Some say it’s to cripple the DA in the Western Cape, others say it’s disgruntled Union members. On the Cape Flats line it’s clear that copper thieves are the main culprits for train sabotage and Metro rail are now building a massive wall from Bontehewel to Netreg Heideveld linked to Nyanga which is costing R70 million rand. This is to separate the line from encroaching shacks and therefoe easy access for copper thieves. Copper thieves are well armed and organised syndicates that attack railway repair staff. They have to work under heavily armed security but no sooner they do a repair it is stolen. Copper thieves are even digging under vendors stalls to access the copper.
metadata.Further information: The situation is so out of hand that the City of Cape Town has been negotiating with PRASA to take over the railway lines because it’s having such a disastrous impact on the Western Cape economy as well as the over- burdened road system. This week they announced that 100 new railway peace officers would be employed. The problem with railway police is that they cannot travel on the trains with any firearms because they are so over- crowded that they will be attacked for their weapons. People are losing their jobs because they are consistently late. 86% of businesses in the Western Cape have said it is affecting their sustainability because they cannot keep up production schedule. The roads are so congested that has a further knock on effect on their bottom -line There should be 88 carriages running but there are only 45. On the central line there should be 33 and they only have 8. People are not only losing their jobs but people are losing their lives. A woman died in the train fire at Ottery station and another woman sustained severe injuries.
